column2: Absalom equips himself with chariots, horses and fifty runners; the selected plural chariots is not reduced to one vehicle.
Early rising and gate-road encounters retain repeated solicitation of men seeking judgment; the city question receives a tribal answer without correction.
Propose Behold before the favourable assessment of the claimant's words; the claim that no royal hearer is available remains Absalom's assertion.
The wish-question about appointment as judge retains every litigant coming to him and his promise of justice.
Approaching obeisance prompts Absalom's hand, grasp and warm kiss; the habitual conduct is not treated as one encounter.
The same treatment of all arriving litigants and making Israel's men's heart his own remain without substituting an unexpressed theft verb.
Forty years remains the selected interval, followed by vows to be fulfilled at Hebron.
column3: The starting point and chronology remain unresolved; four years is not substituted from another witness.

column2: Propose For your servant made a vow to retain the explanatory link. Geshur in Syria, emphatic restoration to Jerusalem and worship remain within Absalom's account.
David's permission in peace is followed by Absalom's rising and going to Hebron; the unnamed departure subject is contextual.
Spies throughout all tribes, the horn signal and proclamation of King Absalom's Hebron reign remain.
Two hundred invited Jerusalem men go in simplicity and without knowledge of the matter; ignorance is expressly stated rather than inferred loyalty to the plot.
Ahithophel the Gelmonite from Gola, the sacrificial occasion and growing conspiracy remain.
column3: The sacrificing subject is inferred as Absalom; names and participial attachment are not harmonized to another account.

column2: The messenger reports Israel's men's hearts following Absalom; this reprises the preceding appropriation of their hearts.
David urges flight for lack of deliverance, repeated haste and avoiding capture, calamity and the city's sword-striking.
The servants defer to the human lord king's choice; here are your servants expresses the presentative.
All the household leaves on foot while ten concubines remain to guard the house; the women are not counted among those departing.
The repeated departure with servants on foot and stopping at the house far away remain.
column3: The house is not assigned a reconstructed official title or exact location.

column2: The full expanded procession retains Chetti, Pelethites, wilderness olive tree, surrounding strong men and warriors, and the later Cherethite/Pelethite/Gittite list with both six-hundred notices.
column3: Repeated counts are not automatically summed into twelve hundred or collapsed into one harmonized roster.

column2: The king addresses Ittai's migration and foreign status as reasons to remain with the king rather than accompany the departure.
column3: The second king's intended referent remains context-dependent; no name is inserted to resolve the political implication.

column2: Both yesterday/today sequences, renewed displacement question, David's indefinite destination and divine mercy-and-truth promise remain in full.
Ittai's oath invokes both the Lord and his human king; death or life does not limit the pledge's place, and servant language remains ordinary human address.
The king permits crossing with him, and Ittai's servants and whole crowd accompany him without an invented troop count.
All the land's loud weeping, repeated Kidron crossing and wilderness-road movement preserve the full selected sequence.
Propose Behold at Zadok's appearance, retaining all Levites, the ark from Baithar, setting it down and Abiathar's ascent until the people finish leaving.
column3: Baithar and the temporal relation of the ascent remain unresolved rather than corrected to a different place or act.

column2: Returning the ark is commanded, while David's own return and seeing its beauty depend on finding favour.
column3: Beauty is the selected ark-related noun; habitation is not substituted.

column2: The alternative divine refusal addresses David as you, and here I am expresses the presentative before yielding to what is good in God's eyes.
The plural Look/Behold introduction is followed by singular return address to Zadok and the two sons of the two priests.
column3: Your in your two sons and with you represents plural addressees; the named parentages prevent treating both sons as Zadok's alone.

column2: Behold, present encampment in Araboth and waiting for word from the plural priestly party remain; an unknown destination is not supplied.
Zadok and Abiathar return the ark to Jerusalem; inherited it stayed there takes the singular final subject as the ark.
column3: A human subject for the singular staying verb is possible; the inherited ark referent remains provisional.

column2: Repeated upward movement, weeping, covered heads and David's bare feet remain, with every accompanying man covering his own head.
The report places Ahithophel among the conspirators; David's prayer asks the Lord his God to scatter counsel without adding archaic pronouns where none are expressed.
Propose and behold at Hushai's arrival, preserving Roos, David's worship, Hushai's Archite identity, torn tunic and earth on his head.
The conditional burden of Hushai crossing with David remains the first side of the contrast with returning to the city.

Propose you will scatter instead of you can scatter for the future result in David's alternative. The entire expanded cover story retains brothers, father behind him, plea to live and repeated servant claims.
column3: These are David's instructions for Hushai's speech, not an assertion by the narrator that Hushai has changed allegiance.

column2: Behold introduces the priests available in the city, and every heard royal-house matter is to be reported to them.
Propose Behold before the two sons, preserving their individual parentages and the plural send/hear instructions to the cooperating group.
Hushai enters the city as Absalom is entering Jerusalem; no invented duration between the arrivals is supplied.
Propose behold at Ziba's meeting with David beyond Roos. The pair of donkeys, two hundred loaves, hundred raisins, hundred dates and wine vessel remain.
column3: No cake, cluster or modern measure is inserted for the fruit quantities; vessel leaves nebel's precise container identity open.

column2: Ziba assigns animals to the royal household, bread/dates to young men and wine to those fainting in the wilderness; he does not repeat every listed provision.
Propose Behold before Ziba's claim that his lord's son stays in Jerusalem expecting his father's kingdom restored.
column3: The nested claim remains Ziba's report and is not promoted to an independently verified motive of Mephibosheth.

column2: Propose Behold, everything belonging to Mephibosheth is yours instead of the added temporal now. The grant and Ziba's bowed wish for favour remain.
Propose Behold at Shimei's appearance from Saul's kin at Bahurim; his Gera parentage and continual cursing remain.
Stones target David and all servants while people and mighty men stand on both sides; no injury outcome is supplied.
Doubled Get out and the bloodshed/lawlessness charges remain Shimei's curse, not a new narrator's verdict.
Propose Behold instead of Now before the calamity claim, retaining Shimei's assertions about Saul's blood, succession and Absalom's kingship.
Abishai's dead-dog insult and proposed beheading remain his speech and intention; the killing is not narrated as performed.
David addresses Zeruiah's sons, orders noninterference and attributes the curse to the Lord's command, then questions who can challenge it.
column3: The attribution remains David's statement; no separately narrated divine speech is invented.

column2: Propose Behold before David's own son's attempt on his life. Belly, the additional Benjaminite and repeated command to let him curse remain.
Perhaps preserves uncertain hope for divine regard and repayment with good for the curse; humiliation is not replaced with guilt or tears.
David's road travel contrasts with Shimei alongside on the mountain, continuously cursing, throwing stones and scattering dust.
Exhaustion and refreshment remain without supplying a place-name absent from this unit.
Absalom and all Israel's men enter Jerusalem with Ahithophel; collective every man is retained without a newly calculated army.
Hushai's Archite and David-companion identifications remain, with the selected single Long live the king proclamation.
Absalom questions loyalty to the companion and failure to depart with him; the repeated companion word remains.

Propose following the chosen one instead of From now on: katopisthen expresses following/behind, not a temporal beginning. Preserve No, but, the Lord/people/Israel's choice, belonging to him and staying with him.
column3: I will follow supplies a finite English predicate for the initial elliptical following phrase. The chosen one's unstated identity and Hushai's strategic ambiguity remain open; the translation does not insert Absalom's name.

column2: Secondly introduces the service question, son relation and comparison with past service before the father; all pronouns remain human.
All of you makes the plural counsel command visible despite Ahithophel being the named addressee; what we should do remains collective.
Ahithophel instructs intercourse with the concubines left guarding the house, predicting public knowledge of paternal disgrace and strengthened supporters.
The rooftop tent and Absalom's going to his father's concubines before all Israel retain the narrated act without inserting a romantic framing.
Former-day counsel's standing as if consulting God's word remains a comparison of its regard to both David and Absalom, not a declaration that every counsel was divine speech.
